data.narrative:
Alsym Energy is a Series C-stage climate and energy company that has raised approximately $110–111M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—alongside a broader comparison universe of nine private companies and one public comparable (Linamar, LNZA).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current value, applies a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $110M base, yielding $187M. Peer-median methodology takes the median valuation of the three same-stage climate-tech comparables at $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. These two approaches diverge materially, reflecting uncertainty around whether Alsym's technology maturity and market position align with median-stage peers or represent earlier-stage risk.

The triangulated range spans $159M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $594M. The wide dispersion—driven by the 4.3x gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods—reflects genuine uncertainty about Alsym's technology validation and capital efficiency relative to the peer cohort. Key sensitivities include the company's demonstrated progress toward commercialization and how its cost and performance metrics compare to KoBold, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy on a technology-adjusted basis.
